cards.text: King Solomon of Israel is on the throne, and the queen of Sheba has just headed home (2 Chronicles 9:12). Now come his riches: 666 talents of gold a year, shields of hammered gold, cups of gold and an ivory throne overlaid with pure gold, like nothing ever made for any kingdom, while the ships of Tarshish bring in ivory, apes and peacocks. Me? Mother Miller bought me out of a bakery's clearance bin for 25 cents.

cards.question: With all this wealth, King Solomon surpasses all the kings of the earth in riches.
All the kings of the earth seek an audience with Solomon. Why do they come?

answers.text: To hear the wisdom God put in his heart
To ask him for help against their enemies
To trade for the gold from his ships

cards.text: Year after year, each visitor brings tribute: silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses and mules. Solomon has 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots and 12,000 horses, reigns over all the kings from the Euphrates to the border of Egypt, and makes silver as common in Jerusalem as stones. Friend, in the junk drawer I got stuck in for years, the only thing that common was DUST.

The rest of Solomon's acts, from beginning to end, are written in the Records of Nathan the Prophet, the Prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite and the Visions of Iddo the Seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat, a man who served Solomon (1 Kings 11:26). Solomon's life fills THREE prophets' books, friend.

cards.question: Solomon reigns in Jerusalem over all Israel. For how long?
After all that gold, Solomon rests with his fathers and is buried in the city of his father ___.
